https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/trm-labs/75699d.description: Build a Safer World. https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/Service.description: It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. Team Join the FinOps Platform Engineering organization within Global Cloud Services (GCS), the team that builds ServiceNow’s internal FinOps Control Tower for cloud cost governance, financial accountability, and unit economics across our multi-cloud estate (AWS, Azure, and GCP). Our organization is structured around three core teams: a Data Engineering and Data Lake team that builds the ELT pipelines landing data into our Iceberg lakehouse and owns data governance; a Platform Services team that operates our open-source platform stack (Trino, Lightdash, Coder, Jupyter, Redash, Hive Metastore/Nessie); and an Analytics Engineering team that builds the dbt data models and supports analysts creating dashboards and data apps. You will own the backlogs for two teams, translate requirements from internal users and FinOps stakeholders into concrete specifications, sequence the roadmap, and drive adoption. Outward, you serve the FinOps practitioners, finance leaders, and capacity planners who depend on data landing reliably and platforms being available when they need them. Define what “production-ready” means for data pipelines and platform services. Sequence the roadmap across both teams so that platform capabilities land ahead of the pipeline and analytics work that depends on them. Gate roadmap phases on clear readiness criteria rather than arbitrary timelines. Ensure each phase builds on a proven foundation. Translate data governance requirements (data classification, access control policies, lineage, retention) into concrete engineering specifications and acceptance criteria. Ensure pipeline reliability is measurable and improving. Define the metrics, track them, and use them to prioritize investment in reliability over new features when needed. Platform Services Product Own requirements and prioritization for platform services alongside the platform services manager. Bring the user and stakeholder perspective; partner on feasibility and sequencing. Define adoption and satisfaction targets for platform services. Understand how internal users experience Trino, Coder, Lightdash, and Jupyter, and drive improvements that reduce friction and increase self-service capability. Advocate for developer experience improvements across the data engineering workflow. Identify pain points in how data engineers use workspaces, CI/CD, notebooks, and query tools, and work with the platform team to resolve them. https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/gamechanger/ca2.description: ABOUT GAMECHANGER: We believe in the life-changing impact youth sports have on and off the field. By building the first and best place to experience the youth sports moments important to our community, we are helping families elevate the next generation through youth sports. So if you love sports and their community-building potential, or building cool products is your sport, GameChanger is the team for you. We are a remote-first, dynamic tech company based in New York City, and we are solving some of the biggest challenges in youth sports today. THE POSITION: GameChanger is launching a Studio team, a small, fast-moving group whose job is to answer one question: is this opportunity worth pursuing? Partnering with our Strategy team, the Studio takes new and emerging business ideas, like expanding into a new sport or entering an international market, and rapidly validates them with real customers. This lets us commit to the right bets faster and stop sitting on promising ideas because we lack evidence. As the founding designer on this team, you'll pair with a product manager to run focused validation sprints. Your toolkit is whatever the question demands: surveys, onsite ethnographic research, concept tests, prototypes in customers' hands, market experiments, or a combination of all of the above. Your output isn't a shipped feature. It's confidence: a clear, evidence-backed recommendation on whether an opportunity deserves deeper investment and handoff to a product team, or whether we should walk away and move on to the next idea. This role is different from a traditional product designer role at GameChanger. You won't have a large supporting cast of researchers, engineers, and analysts embedded on your team. Instead, you'll operate more like a founder, pulling in partners from User Research, Strategy, Product, Engineering, and beyond when you need them. If you're energized by ambiguity, love learning new problem spaces from scratch, and would rather run ten scrappy experiments than polish one feature, this is your team. You’ll report directly to the VP of Design. WHAT YOU'LL DO: - Partner with your PM and the Strategy team to turn emerging business ideas into sharp, testable questions, defining up front what "validated" looks like and what evidence would change our minds. - Own validation sprints end to end: framing the riskiest assumptions, choosing the right method, running the work, and synthesizing what you learn. - Select and execute the right research approach for each question, including surveys, customer interviews, onsite ethnographic research, diary studies, concept and prototype testing, and landing page or demand tests. - Build prototypes at whatever fidelity gets an answer fastest, from paper sketches and Figma flows to functional, AI-assisted coded prototypes you can put in front of real customers. - Use AI tools aggressively across the workflow to build faster, synthesize research at scale, and expand how much the team can evaluate with two people. - Get out of the building. Recruit and engage real coaches, players, families, and prospective customers in new markets and sports. - Deliver clear, honest go/no-go recommendations to leadership, backed by evidence, including the recommendation to not pursue something. - Package validated opportunities (the insight, the evidence, the concept, and the open questions) for a smooth handoff to a product team to build. - Collaborate with User Research, Data & Analytics, Strategy, Product, and Engineering partners as needed to get the job done. - Help define how the Studio operates. As a founding member, you'll shape the team's playbook, cadence, and standards for what "enough confidence" means. WHO YOU ARE: - 5+ years of product design experience, ideally including 0-to-1 work such as early-stage startups, new product incubation, innovation teams, or founding a company of your own. - A strategic thinker who's genuinely curious about the business. You care as much about whether we should build something as how it would work. - Entrepreneurial, self-motivated, and a doer. You don't wait for a brief, a researcher, or a roadmap. You figure out the fastest path to an answer and go. - Comfortable being on a bit of an island. You thrive with high autonomy and ambiguity, and you proactively pull in collaborators rather than waiting for a team to form around you. - A capable researcher in your own right who can plan, recruit for, moderate, and synthesize qualitative and quantitative research without hand-holding. - A versatile prototyper with range. You match fidelity to the question and can move from sketch to interactive prototype to something customers can actually use. - Fluent with (or hungry to master) AI tools for design, prototyping, coding, and research synthesis, and excited about how they let a small team punch far above its weight. - A strong storyteller who can distill messy, ambiguous findings into a crisp narrative and recommendation for executives. - Intellectually honest. You're motivated by finding the truth about an opportunity, not by making every idea look like a winner. - Knowledgeable about (or passionate about learning) sports and the communities around them. BONUS POINTS: - You've founded or worked at an early-stage startup, or on an incubation, venture, or new bets team. - Experience validating international expansion or entirely new market opportunities. - Comfort with lightweight data analysis to size opportunities and interpret experiment results.
